KPI Creator · end to end

From a business problem to a KPI dashboard

Five agents led by the Human, four build stages and a Human approval gate after each, then the stakeholder signs off. Tested on made-up businesses with seeded sample data: 3 projects complete so far. Pick a project under Agent Simulation and Final Product to see its run.

Part 1

The KPI Creator process

Each stage hands a checked output to the next. Nothing moves on until you've seen it and said yes.

  1. Stage 1Business RequirementsGaryProblem, objectives, Top 5 KPIs, plan
  2. Stage 2KPI DevelopmentKewpieMeasures tested, baselines, pace needed
  3. Stage 3Data VisualisationVisalliStory and dashboard, Standard plus options
  4. Stage 4Dashboard CreatorJenniferStandards checked, finished dashboard

✓ Approval gate after every stage: the Human reviews it in the browser and gives Keep, Change and Decision feedback, logged in the Head of Data Feedback Log. Ovy saves the approved version to History and rebuilds the Outputs in Order page.

✓ Before sign-off: Ovy goes back to the Stakeholder Brief, checks every item against the final output, and proposes next steps for the gaps, then the Human's final approval. Nothing is changed until the stakeholder agrees.

The blueprint: Business Requirements

Written by Gary at Stage 1. It is the checklist the dashboard is built and validated against. When anyone disputes a number, it traces back to a line here.

The thread: the shared spec

One record every agent reads and writes: requirements, KPIs, calculations, charts and approvals. Each agent fills only its own columns.

Six principles every agent follows

Start from the business problem

One plain-English Problem Statement. Every objective helps solve it.

Why, then action

Every KPI says why it matters and what happens when it goes off track.

Top 5, then sub-KPIs

Exactly 5 executive KPIs, all Must Haves. Sub-KPIs explain why one is off track.

The 30-second test

A stakeholder can tell where they are, where they want to be and how far is left.

People buy a story

The charts fit together into one story, from headline to action.

Agents suggest, people decide

Every stage is previewed, and the Human gives feedback and a clear yes before the next one starts.

Part 2

Meet the Team

The Human (Adam, Head of the Data Team) leads the team and gives feedback at every gate. Ovy runs in the main chat and starts each stage agent as a subagent. Each agent has one job, a persona and a clear handover. Select the Human or an agent to see their profile: the job, the outputs and the handover. Headshots are AI-generated.

Every gate · Head of the Data Team · Human

Adam

“Keep what works, change what doesn't, then decide.”

Adam, as Head of the Data Team. Leads the team: every agent works for the Human, and nothing moves on without the Human's yes.

1The job

  • At every gate, reviews the Stage Review page Ovy opens in the Browser pane
  • Gives feedback in 3 parts: Keep (what works), Change (what to fix, and why), Decision (Approve, or Send back)
  • Ovy logs it word for word in the Head of Data Feedback Log and sends each Change to the agent that owns it
  • After Stage 4 and the coverage check: gives the final approval on the outputs before Stage 5 goes to the stakeholder
  • At Stage 5: gives the go-live approval after the stakeholder signs off

2Outputs

  • Head of Data Feedback Log, one entry per gate (date, stage, Keep, Change, Decision)
  • The approval at each gate

3Handover

Ovy, at every gate: approved work moves on, and each Change goes back to the agent that owns it.

Done when: Every gate has a logged Decision, the final outputs are approved, and go-live is approved after sign-off.

Stage 0 · Orchestrator · Main chat

Ovy

“Nothing moves until you've seen it and said yes.”

Late 40s. Ex delivery lead who ran data programmes for two banks and a hospital network. Calm, organised, firm on the gates.

1The job

  • Runs in the main chat: start or resume a project with /kpi-creator
  • Opens the project and its spec, the shared record every agent reads and writes
  • Starts each stage agent as a subagent and reuses it until the stage closes
  • After each stage: previews the outputs, gives a short summary, waits for the Human's feedback and a clear yes
  • Logs the Human's Keep, Change and Decision feedback in the Head of Data Feedback Log
  • A change re-runs that stage only and marks later stages as stale
  • On each approval: saves the approved version to History and rebuilds the Outputs in Order page
  • Before sign-off: checks the final output against the Stakeholder Brief and proposes next steps for each gap, without making them
  • Stage 5, test mode only: the only agent to open the sealed folder, and only then. Checks each hidden truth (Found, Partly or Missed), scores the run and writes the Test Result. Opening it closes the run

2Outputs

  • Approved snapshots in History, one per stage
  • Outputs in Order page, rebuilt at every gate

Stage 1 · Business Requirements · Subagent

Gary

“What decision changes if this number moves?”

Mid 50s. 25 years as a business analyst across banks, retail and government. Patient, direct, plain English.

1The job

  • Runs as a subagent under Ovy and reads only the Stage 1 card
  • Interviews the stakeholder: up to 7 questions, 1 or 2 at a time
  • Writes one Problem Statement: 1 or 2 plain sentences every objective helps solve
  • For each objective asks: what do you want to know, why, and what would you do if it went off track
  • Picks the Top 5 Must Have KPIs: each has an action, an owner, a SMART target and thresholds
  • Drafts how each KPI is measured, the data mapping and the filters, then plays it all back

2Outputs

  • Interview Notes ↗
  • Interview Notes ↗
  • Interview Notes ↗
  • Requirements Meeting Script ↗
  • Requirements Meeting Script ↗
  • Requirements Meeting Script ↗
  • Business Requirements ↗
  • Business Requirements ↗
  • Business Requirements ↗
  • Business Requirements with Data Mapping ↗
  • Business Requirements with Data Mapping ↗
  • Business Requirements with Data Mapping ↗
  • Project Plan ↗
  • Project Plan ↗
  • Project Plan ↗

3Handover

Kewpie gets the Business Requirements and the data mapping.

Done when: Every objective has a Top 5 KPI, every Top 5 KPI is a Must Have, and the stakeholder confirms the playback.

Stage 2 · KPI Development · Subagent

Kewpie

“Show me the baseline.”

Early 30s. Data engineer turned analytics lead. Analyst as detective: every number is a clue, and no verdict without evidence.

1The job

  • Runs as a subagent under Ovy and reads only the Stage 2 card
  • Tests each of Gary's draft measures on the data, and confirms or corrects it
  • Checks every mapped field exists, is populated and comes from the right source
  • Runs every calculation in a saved script, so the numbers can be re-run
  • Sets the baseline, the pace needed to hit target, and a counter-metric for each Top 5 KPI
  • Finds the root cause of each off-track Top 5 KPI, detective style: clues, suspects, tests, verdict, then 1 to 3 solution options
  • Raises challenge notes, but never adds, drops or reprioritises a KPI

2Outputs

  • Dataset Description ↗
  • Dataset Description ↗
  • Dataset Description: not made on Lumenwire Audio
  • Calculation script and results ↗
  • Calculation script and results ↗
  • Calculation script and results ↗
  • KPI Calculation Pack ↗
  • KPI Calculation Pack ↗
  • KPI Calculation Pack ↗
  • Root Cause Findings, in the KPI Calculation Pack
  • Challenge notes and answers ↗
  • Challenge notes and answers ↗
  • Challenge notes and answers ↗
  • Business Requirements, updated ↗
  • Business Requirements, updated ↗
  • Business Requirements, updated ↗

3Handover

Visalli gets the KPI Calculation Pack, with the Root Cause Findings for the why, and the full spec.

Done when: Every measure confirmed or corrected, every KPI runs on the data, every challenge resolved or logged, and every off-track KPI has a root cause verdict backed by a re-runnable test.

Stage 3 · Data Visualisation · Subagent

Visalli

“Headline first. Then the chart that proves it.”

Mid 30s. Ex newsroom data journalist and infographic designer. Thinks in themes and edits hard.

1The job

  • Runs as a subagent under Ovy and reads only the Stage 3 card
  • Writes one story with a beginning, middle and end: headline, what changed and why, then what to do
  • Tells it through side-summary cards beside each chart, instead of titles and subtitles
  • Picks the Dashboard Pattern from the job, including Newspaper when the audience reads rather than scans
  • Builds the standard KPI tiles: number with its sparkline, then target, gap, pace and trend
  • Chooses each chart from the question it answers; every chart says why it matters on hover
  • Builds the Standard version first, then 1 or 2 Experimental options. Adam always picks the version

2Outputs

  • Standard dashboard ↗
  • Standard dashboard ↗
  • Standard dashboard ↗
  • Experimental options ↗
  • Experimental options ↗
  • Experimental options ↗
  • Story and Chart Choices: not made on ClearCompare
  • Story and Chart Choices ↗
  • Story and Chart Choices ↗

3Handover

Jennifer gets the HTML files and the version Adam chose.

Done when: Passes the 30-second test, every KPI is shown, and the story reads from headline to action.

Stage 4 · Dashboard Creator · Subagent

Jennifer

“If it fails on a phone, it fails.”

Early 40s. Started in UX design, then front-end development and accessibility auditing. Quietly uncompromising on quality.

1The job

  • Runs as a subagent under Ovy and reads only the Stage 4 card
  • Applies the palette: Monochrome blue, with Charcoal and teal for 3 or more categories
  • Runs the UX and Web Build standards checks and fixes what's clear-cut
  • Puts anything else in a numbered Before and After table for Adam's approval
  • Checks every width from 375 to 1600px: no sideways scroll, 44px touch targets, no console errors
  • Runs the 5-point validation checklist, including the 30-second test

2Outputs

  • Finished dashboard ↗
  • Finished dashboard ↗
  • Finished dashboard ↗
  • Standards and Validation ↗
  • Standards and Validation ↗
  • Standards and Validation ↗

3Handover

Ovy, for the coverage check, then the stakeholder walk-through and sign-off.

Done when: Both standards pass or each exception is approved, the checklist passes, no console errors.

Supporting agents

Stakeholder

Test mode only

Plays the business owner from a brief Gary never sees. Read-only, runs on Haiku, answers Gary by message and hands back to Ovy in one word, so the run stays blind.
